source.title: Generalization of Gibbs and Langevin Monte Carlo Algorithms in the Interpolation Regime
source.authors: Andreas Maurer; Erfan Mirzaei; Massimiliano Pontil

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices and experimental results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests random-label fitting and generalization with SGLD and ULA on neural networks, rather than reproducing the original SGD training procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports random-label and true-label experiments. Figure-only plots show training and test errors across inverse temperatures; the text gives one explicit random-label training-error result. It does not test shuffled or Gaussian inputs, label-noise fractions, regularization necessity, or learning order. Figures 4, 7–13 also plot bounds, which are not rows because they measure the paper's proposed method rather than the claim's behavior.
record.test_reason: The study measures random-label training errors under SGLD and ULA, with matched true-label controls. These results bear on V1 despite using Langevin training and posterior-average errors rather than the original SGD procedure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors derive data-dependent Gibbs bounds stable under approximation, then obtain tight empirical bounds using heuristically calibrated LMC approximations. They explicitly describe calibrated tightness as experimental and transfer to SGD as preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Gibbs posterior analysis and Langevin Monte Carlo algorithms (SGLD and ULA), with a Gaussian prior and temperature sweep; it does not reproduce the original standard SGD procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports poorer random-label fitting for convolutional architectures, especially on MNIST. It also varies dataset, architecture, loss, algorithm, training sample size and inverse temperature across experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: True-label training errors decrease more rapidly across inverse temperatures, and high-temperature errors predict low-temperature generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temperature-dependent training-error profiles distinguish true-label and random-label data under Langevin sampling.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Several displayed training and test error results are available only in plots. The experiments use small sample sizes, and the authors say practical LMC approximations require calibration; calibrated-bound tightness is an experimental finding. The random-label test error is not numerically stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 7–13 include additional single-draw and alternate-setting plots, but their figure-only training/test curves are not separately extracted here because the central Figure 4 conditions and the explicit convolutional qualification capture the reported scope; bounds were excluded because they measure the proposed method. Table 1 and Tables 2–3 report true-label test errors or bounds, not random-label fitting outcomes.

untested.parts: The original SGD recipe and a separately quantified chance-level test-error result are not established by these rows. The main reported fitting errors are posterior averages.
Relative training time and convergence as a function of label-corruption fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Intermediate label-corruption fractions, perfect training fit throughout that sweep, and steady test-error degradation.

Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent interpolation, and whether removing them preserves true-label generalization. The Gaussian prior induces L2 regularization, but no relevant ablation establishes these claims.
Temporal ordering of learning shared patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: Temperature sweeps do not establish training-time learning order or optimization speed. Additional random-label settings in Figures 7–13 are already declared in rows_left_out; their numerical curves cannot be recovered from the supplied text. The study is not an original source for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: The paper uses SGLD or ULA rather than the original SGD recipe; exact test error at chance is only plotted.
